reports.title: The Home Depot Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results;

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2026 Guidance
section: The Company updates its fiscal 2026 guidance.

desk.headline: Sales up 4.9% to $43.4bn, above estimates, and adjusted EPS of $3.86 roughly in line; full-year outlook narrowed with sales growth at the top of the range

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted (non-GAAP); GAAP diluted EPS $3.72 vs $3.62

results: Sales rose 4.9% to $43.4bn, helped by acquisitions; comparable sales grew 2.2% (US also +2.2%), far better than the 0.2% of a year ago.
Shoppers spent more per visit (average ticket +3.0% to $93.09) while transactions slipped 0.5% on a comparable basis.
Margins eased: gross margin fell to 32.8% from 33.4% and adjusted operating margin to 13.0% from 13.3%, as lower-margin acquired businesses grew in the mix.
Adjusted EPS rose 3.2% to $3.86; GAAP EPS was $3.72, up from $3.62. Net earnings were $3.7bn.
Nine-month operating cash flow improved to $15.5bn; dividends paid so far this year total $7.0bn. The company ended the quarter with 2,372 stores.

guidance.summary: Home Depot swapped its full-year ranges for single figures: sales growth now about 4.5% (top of the old 2.5–4.5% range) and comparable sales about 1.4%, but margins are at the low end and EPS growth (about 2% adjusted) sits in the lower half of the old flat-to-4% range.

points: Management said demand is steady and the company is taking market share even though home sales (housing turnover) remain near multi-year lows.
Both professional contractors and DIY shoppers comped positively, with Pro ahead; big-ticket purchases over $1,000 rose 4.5%, led by power tools and appliances.
About half of the higher average ticket came from inflation; fuel, freight, resin and metals costs were higher than planned, but price increases are being kept modest.
Roofing demand is weak after two years of few storms, so SRS's organic growth expectation was cut to low single digits; the margin cut was put down to product and acquisition mix.
Early November trading was said to be in line with the updated guidance; incoming CEO Richard McPhail led the call.
call.source: Investing.com call transcript and The Motley Fool takeaways, 17 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether comparable sales hold near 2% in Q4 as housing turnover stays weak.
Gross and operating margin pressure from acquired businesses (SRS, GMS) and higher input costs.
Roofing and storm-related demand at SRS.
